summary: Zesho Machida worked in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Minobusan Okunoin Shishinkaku as betto (attested 1990) and at Minobusan University as professor emeritus (attested 1996–2001).
Zhao Luo works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He studied under Sen Wang and held a post as a scholar at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).
Zhaohua Yang works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held posts at Stanford University (attested 2007) and Columbia University (faculty, attested 2018), and taught Kevin Buckelew.

Zhe Ji specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He completed a Ph.D. in sociology at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences in 2007 and was an Associate Professor at INALCO (attested 2011–2017).
Zhen Liu is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He earned an MA from the University of Munich by 2005 and an MA from Lanzhou University by 2009.
Zhengyan is a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who studied as a disciple under Yin Shun in 1963. She founded the Tzu Chi Foundation in 1966 and Tzu Chi University in 2000.

Zhenhua (1922–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tianning Buddhist Institute (1947) and under Yin Shun (1952). He taught Chien Y. Hsu and served as manager at Fuyan Buddhist Institute (attested 1992).

Zhihua Yao specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Boston University (~1997–2002) under Malcolm David Eckel, and later held posts at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2003) and The University of Hong Kong (2005).
Zhiru Ng specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned an MA at the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez and a PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello.

Zhiru Shi is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Pomona College (attested 2007–2014).

Zhiyi Yang is a Sinology scholar who earned an undergraduate degree at Peking University and a PhD at Princeton University under Martin Kern. She held posts at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg and Goethe University Frankfurt (attested 2015).

Zhonghui Cui specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. She earned an MA from SOAS and a PhD from The University of Hong Kong, where she later served as a teaching consultant (attested 2013).
Zhongpei Zhang (1934–2017) was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied under Su Bai (~1952–1956). He served as director at the Palace Museum (~1987–1991).

Zhongxin Jiang (1942–2002) specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji (~1960–1965), worked at Peking University (~1965–1978), and served as Associate Professor at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978–2002).
Zhuan Dao (1871–1943) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Tongzhi. He founded Poo Thor Jee in 1911 and Kong Meng San Phor Kark See Monastery in 1920.
Zijie Li is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Komazawa University (attested 2015) and was an appointed DC research fellow at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2015).

Zoltán Gombocz (1877–1935) was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berzsenyi Dániel Gimnázium and Eötvös Loránd University (1895–1900), and taught Lajos Ligeti.

Zong Rinpoche (1905–1984) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. Educated at Ganden Shartse and Gyuto monasteries under Dechen Nyingpo and Trijang Rinpoche, he served as Abbot of Ganden Shartse (1937–1946) and rector of CIHTS (1967–1971).

Zongsan Mou (1909–1995) studied philosophy at Peking University under Shili Xiong. He held professorships at institutions including Tunghai University (~1956–1968), The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~1968–1974), and the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies (~1974–1995).

Zsóka Gelle is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Vienna, where she also held a doctoral college post (2011–2014), alongside Khyentse Fellowships at ELTE and BCBR (2014–2016).
